newsitem.title: UK: UK's Atlantic Telecom to raise 23 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK's Atlantic Telecom to raise 23 mln stg.

text.p: Atlantic Telecom said on Friday it planned to raise 23.2 million stg via a share placing and open offer to fund the development of the group's fixed radio access telephony business in the greater Glasgow region.
The group said it was placing about 20 million shares at 125 pence, equivalent to 25 pence before a one for five consolidation of its share capital.
The group, Britain's only quoted wireless telephone company, said its Glasgow fixed radio access telephony service would be officially launched in the last quarter of 1996.

Formerly Caledonian Media Communications Plc, who have operated cable systems in the UK for over 10 years, Atlantic Telecom said it had also won approval in principle for a Scottish licence allowing it to develop the service across urban Scotland.
The company said that Atlantic Telecom's service would be both attractive to customers and deliver a sustainable competitive advantage.
Atlantic plans to undercut BT or other competitors as it focuses on small and medium-sized businesses as well as higher spending residential customers.

During the initial launch phase, installation is likely to be free for customers, although the company stated: "The directors believe that, over time, service and innovation will replace price as the key means of differentiation."

Atlantic Telecom said early indications were that its trading loss arising from cable operations was broadly in line with expectations, adding that its prospects would become increasingly dependent on the performance of its telephony arm.
"The funds to be realised from the placing and open offer are critical to the development on this business," it said.
The company expects to continue to generate losses and does not expect to pay dividends in the forseeable future.
